items.title: Two weeks on, families wait for DNA answers
items.blurb: Relatives of people missing after the Bhotekoshi floods are turning to DNA testing to identify recovered bodies, but labs are overloaded and under-resourced.

items.title: An algorithm is trying to put names to Nepal’s flood dead
items.blurb: Facial-recognition technology FaceTagr is helping families search for possible matches, but police say DNA testing remains the only reliable option for badly damaged remains.

items.title: Rabi Lamichhane urges action against those targeting flood victims online
items.blurb: The RSP chair says the Bhotekoshi floods should be declared a national climate-related disaster and calls for a special all-party parliamentary committee to oversee the response and long-term recovery.

items.title: ‘You are not alone, Nepal’: UEFA Champions League pays tribute to flood victims
items.blurb: European football’s elite competition will observe a moment of silence and display solidarity banners across all 18 opening-week matches following the late-August disaster in central Nepal.

items.title: Nepal restores power, rebuilds links in flood-hit Rasuwa and Nuwakot
items.blurb: Electricity has returned to more communities as the Nepali Army works to install a temporary bridge after floods destroyed key infrastructure.

items.title: Nepal waives health insurance fees in flood-hit districts
items.blurb: Patients in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading will not have to pay co-payments or show physical insurance cards for three months.

items.title: Water flow returns to normal in Kaski river after temporary blockage
items.blurb: The Kimrong Khola was temporarily blocked on Tuesday, prompting precautionary evacuations downstream, but the blockage began clearing overnight and the river has since returned to its normal flow.

items.title: Global backing grows for Nepal’s climate aid appeal
items.blurb: More than a dozen members of the UN-backed Loss and Damage Fund are pushing for an emergency board meeting to consider Nepal’s request for support after the Bhotekoshi floods.

items.title: Floods disrupt access to healthcare in Rasuwa and Nuwakot
items.blurb: Damaged roads have made hospitals difficult to reach for the affected, including pregnant women.

items.title: Dhunche has relief supplies. Getting aid to flood-hit Rasuwa villages is the problem
items.blurb: Destroyed roads have left communities in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts reliant on helicopters, drones and temporary crossings.

items.title: Nepal looks for grants for flood recovery, but loans may be unavoidable
items.blurb: Officials expect the Post-Disaster Needs Assessment to put flood losses at around 30 percent above the initial estimate. Experts say Nepal may have to turn to soft loans to fill the funding gap.

items.title: Time to move past the basics in disaster response
items.blurb: Assistance must go beyond immediate survival to restore safety, dignity, identity and community connections.

items.title: Arsenal Foundation donates to Nepal flood relief
items.blurb: The Premier League club says it will also pay tribute to flood victims before its Champions League match against Napoli this week.

items.title: Nepal races to rebuild roads and bridges washed away by floods
items.blurb: With 41 bridges destroyed between Rasuwa and Chitwan, authorities are reopening roads and seeking temporary bridges from China and India to restore key links.

items.title: How two men survived nine days in a Nepal flood tunnel
items.blurb: Trapped in an air pocket beneath the wreckage of a hydropower tunnel, two workers endured nine days of darkness, mud and dwindling hope before rescuers heard a faint sound from underground.

items.title: How crypto found a ‘legal’ route into Nepal’s relief efforts
items.blurb: A new US-based channel lets cryptocurrency users donate to Nepal’s disaster fund without the digital assets entering the country, where crypto trading and use are prohibited.

items.title: A flood of bad news leaves Nepal’s tourist hubs eerily quiet
items.blurb: Negative reports about the Bhotekoshi floods, road disruptions, and travel advisories have hit bookings in Pokhara, Chitwan and Lumbini just as the peak tourist season gets underway.
